newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes, sells dlr to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes, sells dlr to support won.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in Friday afternoon trading, selling dollars to support the won against the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
They said the bank began selling dollars as the won fell to a new 83-month low of 856.00 per dollar.
Dealers said the won sharply fell to 856.00, the lowest level in 83 months, affected by the dollar's rise against the Japanese yen on world markets.
The dollar rose to a 47-month high of 120 yen in Tokyo.
The won rose to 854.50 after the central bank's intervention.
